prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1479; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative: On arrival in Houston, Texas, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles. Driver 2 was stopped in the travel lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 1 struck the rear bumper. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel when I arrived, and I confirmed the presence of Driver 1 at the scene. A Passenger was also in the vehicle. Damage to both vehicles is consistent with a low-speed impact of the kind described by the drivers. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and said the pain began shortly after the collision. The impact appeared minor, and the reported injuries seem more serious than the damage would suggest. Photographs taken at the scene show the damage and some details of the positions of the vehicles. No independent witnesses came forward. Both drivers gave statements that match the photographs in most respects. A few old scratches were visible on the rear of Driver 1's vehicle, and it is unclear whether they predate this collision. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy for that vehicle.
